- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.3), model underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–3% per 3-day horizon.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive (e.g., >0.3 in 2–3 days), model delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early days — reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 2–5% to align with observed mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (avg > 0.3) and price is rising, model tends to overforecast — apply 3–5% downward bias to final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative and price is near recent low, model often underestimates rebound — add 2–4% upward bias to next 3–5 days.
